Term1: Hepatitis A and B vaccine information
Text:
## Vaccine route, orders, names
## __________________________
## Route: IM
## Outpatient HepA/B orders:
[3 dose series](orz-set-abx-op-hepatitis-a-b-vaccine-3-dose-series)
[Booster Dose](psczid-hepatitis-a-b-vaccine-booster-dose)
Rapid schedule:
[4 dose series](orz-set-abx-op-hepatitis-a-b-vaccine-accelerated-4-dose-series)
## CPRS name:
HEPATITIS A/HEPATITIS B
VACCINE INJ,SUSP
## Stocked brand name:
Twinrix
## Other names:
Hepatitis A/B Recombinant
(HepA/HepB)
References:
Immunization Action
Coalition,
Summary of Adult
Immunizations, 2021, P2011
Murthy et al. Annals
internal medicine, 2022,
175(3)432-443
<!-- COLUMN 2 -->
## Recommended populations
## __________________________
*All adults who want to be
protected from hepatitis A
and hepatitis B virus
infection.
## HepA Specific:
*People who travel or work
anywhere EXCEPT the U.S.,
most, but not all of
Western Europe, New
Zealand, Australia,
Canada, and Japan.
*People with chronic liver
disease, injecting and
non-injecting drug users,
people who have HIV
infection, men who have
sex with men, people who
are homeless or live in
temporary housing (e.g., a
shelter), people who work
with HAV in lab settings.
*People who anticipate
close personal contact
with an international
adoptee from
a country of high or
intermediate endemicity
during the first 60d
following the adoptee's
arrival in the U.S.
*Postexposure: adults with
recent (within 2wks)
exposure to HAV, give
HepA. Vaccine may be used
in conjunction with IG at
the provider's discretion
in adults older than age
40 or immunocompromised
## HepB Specific
*People age 19-59yrs
*People age 60yrs and older
who want to be protected
from hepatitis B virus
infection and those who are
at risk for hepatitis B
virus infection:
o Chronic liver disease
(e.g., persons with
hepatitis C, cirrhosis,
fatty liver disease,
alcoholic liver disease,
autoimmune hepatitis,
alanine aminotransferase
[ALT] or aspartate
aminotransferase [AST]
level greater than twice
upper limit of normal)
o HIV infection
o Sexual exposure risk
(e.g., sex partners of
hepatitis B surface
antigen [HBsAg]-positive
persons: sexually active
persons not in mutually
monogamous relationships:
persons seeking evaluation
or treatment for a
sexually transmitted
infection: men who have
sex with men)
o Current or recent
injection drug use
o Percutaneous or mucosal
risk for exposure to blood
(e.g., household contacts
of HBsAg-positive persons:
residents and staff of
facilities for
developmentally disabled
persons: health care and
public safety personnel
with reasonably
anticipated risk for
exposure to blood or
blood-contaminated body
fluids: hemodialysis,
peritoneal dialysis, home
dialysis, and predialysis
patients: patients with
diabetes)
o Incarcerated persons
o Travel in countries with
high or intermediate
endemic hepatitis B
patient is chronically
infected, assure
appropriate disease
management. For sex
partners and household
contacts of HBsAg-positive
people, provide serologic
screening and administer
initial dose of HepB
vaccine at same visit.
*Serologic testing is
recommended 1 to 2 months
after the final dose of
the primary vaccine series
and annually to determine
the need for booster
doses. Persons with anti-
HBs concentrations of <10
milliunits/mL should
receive a booster dose
NOTE: Provide serologic
screening for immigrants
from endemic areas. If
patient is chronically
infected, assure
appropriate disease
management. For sex
partners and household
contacts of HBsAg-positive
people, provide serologic
screening and administer
initial dose of HepB
vaccine at same visit.
<!-- COLUMN 3 -->
## Administration Schedule
## __________________________
*Standard Schedule: Give 3
doses on a 0, 1, 6-month
schedule.
*Rapid Schedule: Give 4
doses on a 0, 1wk, 3wks,
and 1yr schedule. Must
receive all dose for long
term protection.
<!-- COLUMN 4 -->
## Contraindications/Precautions
## __________________________
## Contraindications:
History of severe allergic
reaction (e.g.,
anaphylaxis) to a previous
dose or a vaccine
component.
## Precautions:
Moderate or severe acute
illness with or
without fever.
